content:
Hello everyone,

I've recently tried to start getting into Lean and using Mathlib4.

I'm using VS Code and every time I start a Lean file with "import Mathlib" it takes a very long to where it says "updating", it can take anywhere between 20 to 30 mins before it finishes.

It does this every time I use Lean in VS code (not just the first time).

Was wondering if anyone could help me sort this out so I can get to formalizing mathematics haha.

Thanks in advance for any help,
Gavin.

So for my setup I'm using VS Code on my PC, I downloaded the Lean extension through VS Code. Then in VS Code I have clicked the "forall" symbol and I clicked "New Project" then "Create Project Using Mathlib". It then takes a while and says its downloading lake and Elan and so forth. Then once it says something like "Project setup complete" if I make a .lean document in the project folder, I'll start it with "import Mathlib" and then the problem starts.

Click the forall symbol, then "Project Actions...", then "Fetch Mathlib Build Cache"
You may need to "Restart Server" afterwards, and "Restart File"

Hi I have just tried this and it looks like it hasn't worked, it said the "Fetch Mathlib Build Cache" ran succesfully and I have restarted the server and file but when I load them again I still get the spinning "updating" and its taking 20 mins to load.
"updating" is a strange message; could you share a screenshot?
Do you have 8 gigs of ram or less?
Are you running Windows and do you have antivirus software installed? (If so, excluding the directory where mathlib is placed from scanning can speed up things a lot.)

I have circled in red the small spinning wheel that says "Updating" (its only says this when i hover the cursor over it) after it loads the Lean server. This is the screen that it sits at for sometimes 20 mins.

I have 16 gigs of ram.

Yes I am running windows, I will check the antivirus thing now.
Close the window, run lake exe cache get in the terminal and reopen VS Code
Unfortunately I have tried this already (a few times actually) and still the same.
How long does it take to run lake build <your_file>?
